answer: A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 276 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The basalt detector writes to trellis, and dawn makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 176 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
